question: Why are action and the other powers not different from consciousness?
premises: The powers of action and so on are not more than the nature of consciousness.
They cannot be joined to a non-conscious form.
No separate bearer of these powers can be established.
inference: Therefore the powers beginning with action are nothing other than consciousness itself.
uncertainties: The exact force of saṃvidrūpādhikā may be read as exceeding or as additional to consciousness-form.
plain_english: The powers such as action are not anything beyond consciousness. They cannot be non-conscious, and no separate owner of them can be proved. So they are of the nature of consciousness.
